model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: Model identity is the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, taken from the session environment (claude-opus-5[1m], Opus 5 with 1M context), not the agent definition's template text, which names a different model.

issues_detected.description: Version ordering is internally contradictory as presented. The record carries version '2.0' for the June 2026 release, while version_access.versions_available states that the June 2025 and October 2025 releases were both at version 2.1. Read as one list, the current release appears to regress two minor versions behind its own predecessors. Each release holds a distinct DOI with its own Dataverse version counter, so the values are not strictly impossible, but nothing in the record tells a reader that, and the citation's 'V2' adds a third numbering.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that the version number is the Dataverse version counter of this DOI rather than a project-wide release sequence, or carry the release-series designation ('June 2026 Data Release') as the version and record the Dataverse counter separately

issues_detected.description: preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools describe the MuSIC cell-map construction pipeline end to end (node2vec PPI embedding, DenseNet-121 image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GPT-4 assembly naming via the Gene Set AI pipeline). Those steps produce computed cell maps, which this release explicitly does not contain: known_limitations records 'It does not contain predicted cell maps' and intended_uses says the release 'is most suitable for bioinformatics analysis of the individual datasets'. So the processing documented is downstream of the delivered files, not applied to them, and a reuser still cannot tell how the released mass-spectrometry tables and image archives were processed.
issues_detected.recommendation: Separate the per-modality processing that produced the ten delivered archives (spectral search, elution-profile scoring, image segmentation and QC, guide assignment and count-matrix generation) from the downstream MuSIC map-building pipeline, and label the latter as applying to future releases

issues_detected.description: created_on is recorded as 2025-02-27, sixteen months before issued (2026-06-17), and the record's own source_caveats states that this Dataverse 'Data Creation Date' is 'carried unchanged across the March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, and June 2026 release records in the bundle and is unlikely to be specific to this release's content'. A value the record itself judges non-specific still occupies the dataset-level creation date, where a consumer will read it as when this release's content was created.
issues_detected.recommendation: Omit created_on as the record omits last_updated_on for the same reason, or move the Dataverse-carried date into a note so it is not read as this release's creation date

issues_detected.description: Distribution format is documented only at container level. distribution_formats gives 'ZIP Archive' with media_type application/zip and 'RO-Crate', and every file_collection records compression: zip, but no slot states what the archives contain: no image format for the 12.6 GB of confocal data, no mass-spectrometry format for the SEC-MS and AP-MS packages, no matrix or sequence format for the Perturb-seq atlas, and no character encoding anywhere. The one format statement below container level is raw_data_sources[1].raw_data_format, 'Confocal microscopy image with four color channels', which describes structure rather than a named standard.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record the per-archive payload formats (for example OME-TIFF or PNG for imaging, mzML or the search-engine output format for mass spectrometry, MTX/H5AD or FASTQ for Perturb-seq) and a character encoding for the tabular members

issues_detected.description: The dedicated download_url slot is unused. The resolvable deposit link is carried inside distribution_formats[0].access_urls, and file_collections give path values that are bare filenames rather than URLs, so an automated client following the schema's own download slot finds nothing.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate download_url with the Dataverse persistent URL already present in access_urls, and give each file collection a resolvable Data Access API URL alongside its path

issues_detected.description: page resolves to the CM4AI project's release index (https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/) rather than to the landing page of the DOI this record identifies. The deposit landing page for doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C exists in the record but sits in distribution_formats access_urls, so the identifier and the landing page are documented in different places.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set page to the Dataverse landing page for this DOI and keep the project release index as an external resource

issues_detected.description: principal_investigator is nested inside the final creator entry (Trey Ideker) at the same level as that person's name and affiliations, and its value restates that same person. A dataset-level role is expressed as a property of one creator, so a consumer walking the creators list finds a role assertion in a position where a person's own attributes are expected.
issues_detected.recommendation: Lift principal_investigator to the dataset level, or express the role through a typed contributor role on the creator entry

issues_detected.description: publisher is a bare ROR CURIE (ROR:0153tk833) with no human-readable name at that slot. The identifier is correct and machine-actionable for the University of Virginia, but a reader of the publisher field alone learns neither the institution nor that the repository is the University of Virginia Dataverse; both are recoverable only from the citation and the access URL.
issues_detected.recommendation: Carry the publisher name alongside the ROR identifier, and name the repository (University of Virginia Dataverse) rather than only the institution

issues_detected.description: Rubric-structural note rather than a defect of the record: Element 4 is scored, not excluded, because the governance trigger is met on Element 2 fields (regulatory_restrictions is populated and names a governance_committee_contact, and a Data Access Committee with an access_review_process supervises distribution and dual licensing). The human-subject trigger is not met, so the three participant sub-elements (privacy and re-identification risk, informed consent, vulnerable populations and compensation) score 0 for content that cannot exist for measurements on established cell lines. Three of the record's eleven lost points are this artifact.
issues_detected.recommendation: No record change is warranted. Read Element 4 for this record as the two ethics sub-elements it can satisfy, both of which it does

issues_detected.description: known_biases carries a single entry, representation_bias, covering the fact that commercial cell lines do not represent population-wide biological variation. The record documents but does not categorise two further selection axes it states elsewhere: sampling_strategies records protein-level targeting of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes, and known_limitations records that the SEC-MS, imaging and Perturb-seq modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets. Both are selection biases that shape any model trained on the release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add selection_bias entries for the targeted protein panel and for the incomplete cross-modality protein overlap, with affected_subsets naming the modalities

semantic_insights: DOI 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C is well formed and its prefix (10.18130) is the registrar prefix of the University of Virginia Dataverse, which agrees with publisher ROR:0153tk833 (University of Virginia), with the citation's 'University of Virginia Dataverse', with the access URL at dataverse.lib.virginia.edu and with the retention statement naming the same repository. Five identity signals, one institution.

The four prior-release DOIs in related_datasets (K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX, DXWOS5) all share the 10.18130/V3 prefix and path form of this record's own DOI, and both publication DOIs (10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and 10.1101/2024.11.03.621734) are valid Cold Spring Harbor bioRxiv identifiers.

The cell lines carry correct Cellosaurus RRIDs: RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J. The rubric names the SCR_ and AB_ namespaces; CVCL_ is the legitimate namespace for cell lines and is the semantically right choice here.

Grant identifiers follow NIH patterns: 1OT2OD032742-01 with core project number OT2OD032742 and supplement 3OT2OD032742-01S2 for the Functional Genomics award, and 5U54HG012513-02 for the Bridge2AI Bridge Center. The OT2 other-transaction activity code is the correct one for a Bridge2AI data generation project, and the recorded project period (2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31) is consistent with an update schedule running to November 2026.

The de-identification claim is semantically appropriate to the data type rather than borrowed from a clinical template. It does not assert HIPAA Safe Harbor or k-anonymity, which would be meaningless here; it states that the data are non-clinical, drawn from tissue culture, and cannot be matched to a human subject with current knowledge. The 'with current knowledge' qualifier is a genuine risk-horizon caveat rather than an absolute claim.

Three independent negative declarations agree and each carries a reason: confidential_elements present false, sensitive_elements present false, content_warnings present false, alongside human_subject_research involves_human_subjects false and direct_collection is_direct false. The record answers these questions rather than leaving them empty, which is the harder and more useful behaviour.

Numeric claims reconcile across slots. The 464 proteins imaged per condition appear identically in instances, in subpopulations.distribution and in all three immunofluorescence file descriptions; the 11,739 targeted genes appear in sampling_strategies, in instances and in the Perturb-seq atlas description; and total_file_count of 10 matches exactly the ten entries in file_collections.

Conflicts between sources are declared rather than silently resolved. The 563-versus-464 protein count across release pages is recorded with the ranking that decided it, and Andrej Sali's affiliation carries a source_caveats note stating that the release metadata says UC San Diego while the preprint says UC San Francisco. A reader can audit both decisions.

The reuse guidance is coherent across three slots that could easily have contradicted each other: intended_uses says the release suits bioinformatics analysis of individual datasets, discouraged_uses says not to treat it as a complete cell-map resource, and known_limitations gives the reason, that computed maps are absent from this interim release. The same is true of the embargo, which appears consistently in known_limitations, external_resources restrictions and third_party_sharing.

The licence chain is internally consistent end to end: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 in license and license_and_use_terms, data_use_permission no_commercial_use, a prohibited_uses entry citing that licence, and ip_restrictions naming the copyright holders (Regents of the University of California, with Stanford holding the spatial proteomics raw images) and the negotiation route for commercial use.

correctness_validations.doi_format: valid (10.18130/V3/HIGT4C carries the University of Virginia Dataverse registrar prefix and agrees with publisher, citation, access URL and retention statement; four prior-release DOIs share the prefix and path form; both publication DOIs are valid bioRxiv identifiers)
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid (1OT2OD032742-01 with core number OT2OD032742 and supplement 3OT2OD032742-01S2, and 5U54HG012513-02, all match NIH activity-code patterns; the third funder is the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia, correctly recorded as a named fund in notes rather than forced into an award-number form)
correctness_validations.rrid_format: valid_in_prose (RRID:CVCL_0419 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 are correct Cellosaurus identifiers for MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J, but they appear inside direct_collection free text rather than in an identifier slot, so they are not machine-retrievable)
correctness_validations.url_validity: all_well_formed_with_gaps (cm4ai.org, dataverse.lib.virginia.edu, github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline, cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, fairscape.github.io and integrativemodeling.org are all well formed and plausible; the MassIVE deposits, the SRA BioProject and the Figshare atlas are named without URLs or accession numbers, so those external deposits cannot be resolved from the record)
correctness_validations.orcid_format: valid (over forty ORCID CURIEs across creators, ethical_reviews, data_governance and license contacts, all matching the 16-digit checksummed form including the 0009- prefixes for recently issued identifiers)
correctness_validations.version_ordering: inconsistent_as_presented (version 2.0 for this release sits against prior releases listed at 2.1 in version_access, with the citation giving V2; see the medium-severity issue)

elements.name: Dataset Discovery and Identification
elements.description: Can a user or system discover and uniquely identify this dataset?

sub_elements.name: Persistent Identifier (DOI, RRID, or URI)
sub_elements.evidence: id: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C; version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Well-formed DOI whose 10.18130 prefix is the University of Virginia Dataverse registrar prefix, agreeing with the publisher ROR, the citation, the access URL and the preservation statement. The id is a CURIE rather than a resolver URL, which is the identifier form the schema asks for.

sub_elements.name: Dataset Title and Description Completeness
sub_elements.evidence: title: 'Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence - June 2026 Data Release (Beta)'; description of roughly 1,900 characters naming the Bridge2AI Functional Genomics Grand Challenge, the four assay modalities, both cell lines with their perturbations and differentiation states, the per-modality condition coverage, the RO-Crate and FAIRSCAPE packaging, the three-pillar six-module project structure and the nine collaborating institutions
sub_elements.quality_note: Far above the 200-character threshold and specific throughout. It resolves which modality covers which condition rather than listing modalities in the abstract, and every modality it names reappears in a structured slot lower down.

sub_elements.name: Keywords or Tags for Searchability
sub_elements.evidence: keywords: 30 entries spanning modality (AP-MS, SEC-MS, perturb-seq, scRNAseq, subcellular imaging, size exclusion chromatography), substrate (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J, iPSC, neuron, cardiomyocyte, NPC), perturbagen (paclitaxel, vorinostat, CRISPR/Cas9), domain (breast cancer, protein-protein interaction, protein localization) and programme (Bridge2AI, CM4AI, AI, machine learning)
sub_elements.quality_note: Six times the five-keyword threshold, with expanded terms and their abbreviations paired throughout (affinity purification and AP-MS, neural progenitor cell and NPC, perturbation sequencing and perturb-seq), so the record is findable by either form.

sub_elements.name: Landing Page and Resources (page, hierarchical resources)
sub_elements.evidence: page: https://cm4ai.org/data-releases/; file_collections: ten entries each carrying id, name, collection_type, path, compression and a description with the listed size, publication date and MD5 checksum; distribution_formats[0].access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable landing page plus a genuinely enumerated resource inventory with checksums and per-file publication dates, enough for a downloader to verify what they received. The page points at the project release index rather than the DOI landing page, which is recorded as a low-severity issue; the deposit landing page is present under access_urls.

sub_elements.name: Hierarchical Structure (parent datasets, relationships)
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four is_new_version_of relations to the October 2025, June 2025, March 2025 and May 2024 releases, each with a DOI target and title, plus is_described_by to the CM4AI preprint and is_referenced_by to the perturbation atlas preprint; version_access.versions_available narrates the same release chain with version numbers
sub_elements.quality_note: Six typed relations with resolvable DOI targets, covering both the release lineage and the describing literature. The chain is expressed twice, as typed relations and as a version narrative, and the two agree on membership.

elements.name: Dataset Access and Retrieval
elements.description: Can the dataset and its associated resources be located, accessed, and downloaded?

sub_elements.name: Access Policy and IP Restrictions Defined
sub_elements.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms spelling out CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 obligations (credit, licence link, change indication, non-commercial, share-alike) with data_use_permission: no_commercial_use and a named contact; ip_restrictions.restrictions naming the Regents of the University of California as copyright holder, the Board of Trustees of the Leland Stanford Junior University for spatial proteomics raw images, and the commercial negotiation route
sub_elements.quality_note: The licence is not merely named but unpacked into its obligations, and the intellectual-property statement is unusually precise in splitting copyright by data package rather than asserting a single holder.

sub_elements.name: Regulatory Restrictions and Confidentiality Level Specified
sub_elements.evidence: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions: 'The release records FDA Regulated: No'; hipaa_compliant: not_applicable; governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486); confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present false with details recording Human Subjects No, De-identified Samples Yes, FDA Regulated No
sub_elements.quality_note: The regulatory posture is stated positively rather than left blank: no FDA regulation, HIPAA not applicable, no confidential elements, with a named governance contact. hipaa_compliant: not_applicable is the semantically correct value for non-clinical cell-line data, where 'compliant' would be a category error. No confidentiality_level slot is used, so the classification is carried in prose.

sub_elements.name: Download URL or Platform Link Available
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats[0].access_urls: https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, with notes stating that individual files below the download size limit may be downloaded directly and that the Data Access API is available for programmatic access
sub_elements.quality_note: A resolvable deposit link plus explicit access instructions covering both interactive and programmatic routes, which is what the sub-element asks for. The dedicated download_url slot is unused and file_collections carry bare filenames as path rather than URLs, recorded as a low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Distribution Formats and File Types Specified
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: format 'ZIP Archive' with media_type application/zip, and format 'RO-Crate' noted as the AI-ready packaging produced with FAIRSCAPE; every file_collection records compression: zip; conforms_to: RO-Crate
sub_elements.quality_note: Format and MIME type are both given and RO-Crate is a real community packaging standard, which satisfies this sub-element. The specification stops at the container, so what sits inside the archives is undocumented; that limitation is where Element 3 sub-element 2 fails and is recorded as a medium-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets and External Resources Linked
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: six typed relations with DOI targets; external_resources: eleven entries covering the four MassIVE mass-spectrometry deposits, the SRA BioProject, the Figshare CRISPRi atlas, the embargoed Perturb-seq components with an explicit restrictions field, the cm4ai.org portal, the Cell Mapping Toolkit at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with readthedocs documentation, FAIRSCAPE at fairscape.github.io under the MIT licence, and the Integrative Modeling Platform
sub_elements.quality_note: Both slots are richly populated and the archival flag distinguishes preserved deposits from live documentation. Software resources carry URLs; the repository deposits are named without accessions or URLs, which is recorded under url_validity.

elements.name: Data Reuse and Interoperability
elements.description: Is sufficient information provided to reuse and integrate the dataset with others?

sub_elements.name: License Terms Allow Reuse
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met: distribution_formats is populated with a format and media type, access_urls resolves to the University of Virginia Dataverse deposit, and the licence explicitly permits sharing and adaptation
sub_elements.evidence: license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'Users are free to share and adapt the material, provided appropriate credit is given, a link to the license is provided, changes are indicated, the material is not used for commercial purposes, and contributions are distributed under the same license'
sub_elements.quality_note: A named standard licence with its permissions and conditions written out, and the one restriction it imposes is carried through consistently into prohibited_uses and ip_restrictions. A reuser can determine what they may do without leaving the record.

sub_elements.name: Data Formats Are Standardized (encoding, format)
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: distribution_formats: 'ZIP Archive' (application/zip) and 'RO-Crate'; no format or encoding slot at dataset level; the only sub-container format statement is raw_data_sources[1].raw_data_format: 'Confocal microscopy image with four color channels'
sub_elements.quality_note: Fails on the payload rather than the package. RO-Crate is a genuine standard and is properly declared, but a reuser opening 12.6 GB of imaging archives, two mass-spectrometry packages and a Perturb-seq atlas learns only that all ten are ZIPs. No named scientific format (OME-TIFF, mzML, MTX, FASTQ) and no character encoding appears anywhere, so the archives cannot be integrated with other data without downloading them first.

sub_elements.name: Schema or Ontology Conformance Stated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; ontology CURIEs in use throughout: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 and 63, B2AI_TOPIC:12, 15 and 26, ROR:0153tk833, forty-plus ORCID identifiers, RRID:CVCL_0419 and CVCL_B5P3
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance is asserted at three levels, packaging standard, metadata schema and class, with a resolvable schema URI. Beyond the declarations the record actually uses controlled identifiers for substrates, topics, organisations, people and cell lines, so the conformance claim is demonstrated rather than only stated.

sub_elements.name: Variable Metadata with Identifiers Defined
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: No variables slot; is_tabular: false; the nearest content is instances entries carrying data_substrate and data_topic CURIEs and prose notes, and subsets carrying ids and descriptions
sub_elements.quality_note: No variable-level metadata exists. is_tabular: false means column definitions are partly beside the point for imaging and mass-spectrometry archives, but the non-tabular equivalent is also missing: no per-file field descriptions for the SEC-MS elution tables, the AP-MS interaction records or the Perturb-seq count matrices. The one exception is the imaging channel semantics described in prose, credited in Element 5.

sub_elements.name: Use Guidance Provided (intended, prohibited uses)
sub_elements.evidence: intended_uses: five entries with use_category and usage_notes (AI-ready research data, AI model training, cellular process analysis, perturbation and disease-context analysis, bioinformatics analysis of component datasets); prohibited_uses: two entries (clinical decision-making without regulatory oversight, commercial use without separate licensing); discouraged_uses: two entries (use without domain expertise, use as a complete cell-map resource)
sub_elements.quality_note: All three registers are populated and they are informative rather than boilerplate. The discouraged uses are the most useful part: they tell a prospective user what this interim release will disappoint them at, which is a harder disclosure than listing what it is good for.

elements.name: Ethical Use and Privacy Safeguards
elements.description: Does the dataset provide clear information about consent, privacy, and ethical oversight?

sub_elements.name: IRB or Ethics Review and Data Protection Impact
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Governance trigger met on Element 2 fields, not on Element 4's own. regulatory_restrictions is populated and carries governance_committee_contact: Jillian Parker (ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486), and the record documents a CM4AI Data Access Committee with an access_review_process supervising dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use. The human-subject trigger is not met: Element 1 description and keywords name established cell lines and their perturbations rather than participants, and Element 8 collection_mechanisms describe assays on cultured cells with no recruitment. Under the ambiguity rule a borderline governance condition resolves to applicable.
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, the first describing the Ethics Module's plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access supervision, balancing data openness against intellectual-property protection and commercialisation monitoring, with contact Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801); the second naming Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153), Simon Fraser University; human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false with notes on the ethical sourcing of both cell lines; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact populated
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics oversight is documented substantively and with attributable contacts, which is voluntary here since no human-subject research is involved. The Ethics Module's remit is described as a real function with a scope rather than asserted as an approval. No data protection impact assessment appears, which is coherent for non-clinical cell-line data.

sub_elements.name: Deidentification Method Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance determination on Element 2 fields
sub_elements.evidence: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present: false; deidentification_details: 'The release records De-identified Samples: Yes. CM4AI data are distinctive within Bridge2AI in that they are non-clinical (from tissue cultures) and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject.'
sub_elements.quality_note: No formal method such as Safe Harbor or k-anonymity is named, and correctly so: none was applied because the measurements were never identifiable. The record states the basis for the claim and qualifies it with 'with current knowledge', which is a more honest formulation than an unconditional assertion. That is complete enough for a reuser to know whether linkage risk exists.

sub_elements.name: Privacy Protections and Re-identification Risk Assessment
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance determination on Element 2 fields
sub_elements.evidence: No participant_privacy slot and no reidentification_risk field anywhere in the record. The nearest content is sensitive_elements.sensitivity_details and the is_deidentified rationale already credited under sub-element 2
sub_elements.quality_note: The linkage statement that would form the core of a re-identification assessment exists, but it sits in is_deidentified and is credited there; nothing describes privacy protections as such, and no risk assessment is carried out under the slot intended for it. This is a structural zero for a dataset with no participants to protect, not a documentation failure, and it is flagged as a rubric artifact in the semantic analysis.

sub_elements.name: Informed Consent Obtained from Participants
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance determination on Element 2 fields; note that the separate human-subject trigger is explicitly negative here, since direct_collection records is_direct: false and 'Data were not collected from human subjects'
sub_elements.evidence: No informed_consent slot. The closest content is human_subject_research.notes recording that both lines were ethically sourced, MDA-MB-468 from ATCC and KOLF2.1J from the HipSci resource under a simple MTA for not-for-profit organisations
sub_elements.quality_note: No consent process exists to document for assays on established commercial cell lines, so this scores 0 on applicability arithmetic rather than on a gap the record could close. The record does address the adjacent question, the provenance and access terms of the source lines, which is the meaningful analogue.

sub_elements.name: Vulnerable Populations and Compensation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same governance determination on Element 2 fields
sub_elements.evidence: No at_risk_populations slot and no participant_compensation slot
sub_elements.quality_note: There are no participants to protect or compensate. Scored 0 rather than excluded because the governance condition, not the human-subject condition, is what makes Element 4 applicable, and that condition gates all five sub-elements. Counted among the three artifact points identified in the semantic analysis.

elements.name: Data Composition and Structure
elements.description: Can the dataset's structure, modality, and population be understood from metadata?

sub_elements.name: Cohort or Subpopulations Characteristics Described
sub_elements.evidence: subpopulations: identification by cell type and treatment condition, enumerating three MDA-MB-468 conditions and four KOLF2.1J states, with a distribution field mapping each modality onto those conditions; subsets: seven entries each with id, name, description and is_subpopulation: true; sampling_strategies.source_data describing MDA-MB-468 as a triple negative line from a pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma, and KOLF2.1J as derived from a healthy male Northern European donor
sub_elements.quality_note: Population structure is given at three levels: the biological substrates with their donor characteristics, the seven experimental subpopulations as addressable subsets with their own identifiers, and the modality coverage of each. The donor descriptions matter for representativeness and are exactly what the bias entry later draws on.

sub_elements.name: Number of Instances or Samples Reported
sub_elements.evidence: total_file_count: 10 matching ten file_collections entries; 464 proteins of interest imaged per treatment condition, stated in instances, subpopulations.distribution and all three imaging file descriptions; 11,739 targeted genes in the CRISPRi atlas; per-file listed sizes from 30.2 KB to 4.6 GB; instances[2].notes: 'The bundle states the number of targeted genes; it does not state the number of profiled cells'
sub_elements.quality_note: Counts are specific, cross-checked across slots and reconcile exactly with the file inventory. The stronger signal is the declared gap: rather than estimating a cell count, the record names the number it does not have. A reader can tell what is measured from what is unknown.

sub_elements.name: Variable-Level Metadata and Tabular Flag
sub_elements.evidence: is_tabular: false is present and correct; no variables slot; the nearest content is instances[0].notes describing the four image channels (protein of interest green, nucleus DAPI blue, endoplasmic reticulum calreticulin yellow, microtubules tubulin red), repeated in acquisition_methods
sub_elements.quality_note: The tabular flag is present and semantically right for a release of image and mass-spectrometry archives, but it is the only half of this sub-element satisfied. The imaging channel semantics amount to a real variable-level description for one modality of four; nothing equivalent exists for SEC-MS elution profiles, AP-MS interaction records or the Perturb-seq atlas, and no data dictionary is provided.

sub_elements.name: Data Topics or Conditions Represented
sub_elements.evidence: instances: three typed entries carrying data_topic CURIEs B2AI_TOPIC:15, 26 and 12 and data_substrate CURIEs B2AI_SUBSTRATE:19 and 63; description naming cancer, neuropsychiatric and cardiac disorders as the disease contexts; subsets enumerating the seven cell-type and treatment conditions
sub_elements.quality_note: Topics are expressed as controlled Bridge2AI ontology terms rather than free text, so they are machine-comparable with other Bridge2AI records, and the disease contexts and perturbation conditions are enumerated in prose alongside them.

sub_elements.name: Data Quality Issues and Anomalies Documented
sub_elements.evidence: sampling_strategies: two entries with is_sample: true, is_random: false, is_representative: false and why_not_representative stating that commercial de-identified cell lines do not represent population-wide biological variation, plus the targeted selection of two disease-relevant lines and of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes; cleaning_strategies recording that single-cell CRISPR screen data from MDA-MB-468 and undifferentiated KOLF2.1J were undergoing quality control at the time of the preprint; known_limitations recording incompletely overlapping protein sets across modalities
sub_elements.quality_note: The sampling strategy is fully characterised with explicit non-random and non-representative flags and a stated reason, which is the substantive part of this sub-element. The named anomalies and missing_data_documentation slots are unused, so quality caveats reach the reader through the limitation slots instead, and no per-file anomaly is documented.

elements.name: Data Provenance and Version Tracking
elements.description: Can a user determine dataset versions, update history, and provenance?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Version Number Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met via populated distribution_formats, a resolvable deposit URL and a reuse-permitting licence
sub_elements.evidence: version: '2.0'; citation records 'V2'; status: Beta
sub_elements.quality_note: A version number is present and quoted as a string, which is the correct temporal form. It is undermined in interpretation rather than in presence: version_access lists two earlier releases at 2.1, so the numbering reads as a regression, recorded as a medium-severity consistency issue.

sub_elements.name: Version Access Methods Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: version_access.versions_available enumerating the June 2026 release at 2.0, the May 2024 release, the March 2025 release at 1.4, and the June 2025 and October 2025 releases at 2.1, and stating that version history is maintained in the University of Virginia Dataverse; latest_version_doi: doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: Every prior release is reachable: named with its version, dated in distribution_dates and carrying a resolvable DOI in related_datasets, with the repository holding the history identified. A user wanting an earlier release knows both which one they want and where to get it.

sub_elements.name: Change Descriptions and Errata Provided
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: No errata slot and no release_notes slot; updates carries cadence rather than content; related_datasets entries name the predecessor releases without stating what changed; the only difference statement anywhere is the note that the May 2024 release is 'Referenced as the May 2024 release in the CM4AI preprint's Data and Software Availability Statement'
sub_elements.quality_note: The release chain is enumerated but never differenced. Nothing tells a user of the October 2025 release what the June 2026 release adds, corrects or withdraws, and no errata are recorded against any release. For a quarterly-updating dataset with five releases this is the most consequential gap in the record.

sub_elements.name: Update Schedule or Frequency Indicated
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: updates.frequency: quarterly; update_details: 'The dataset will be regularly updated and augmented through the end of the project in November 2026, with updates on a quarterly basis'; known_limitations recording that embargoed Perturb-seq data for KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 are expected to become available
sub_elements.quality_note: Cadence, horizon and the specific content expected in future updates are all stated, and the release dates in distribution_dates are broadly consistent with the declared quarterly rhythm. A user can judge both when to re-check and what to re-check for.

sub_elements.name: Provenance and Source Derivation Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: raw_data_sources: two entries with source_type 'laboratory deposition archive' for the Krogan Laboratory PPI networks and the Lundberg Laboratory immunofluorescence images; raw_sources: four entries naming the MassIVE deposits for iPSC and cancer-cell mass spectrometry, the SRA deposit via NCBI BioProject for Perturb-seq raw sequences, and the Figshare CRISPRi atlas; description and distribution_formats recording RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs produced under FAIRSCAPE
sub_elements.quality_note: Derivation is traced back to the originating laboratories and forward to the public archives holding the raw data, and the packaging carries machine-readable provenance graphs. The named was_derived_from and release_notes slots are unused, and the external deposits are named without accessions, so the trail is followable by a human but not automatically.

elements.name: Scientific Motivation and Funding Transparency
elements.description: Does the metadata clearly state why the dataset exists and who funded it?

sub_elements.name: Motivation or Purpose for Dataset Creation
sub_elements.evidence: purposes: four entries covering machine-readable hierarchical cell-architecture maps as AI-ready data, mapping spatiotemporal cell architecture toward interpretable genotype-phenotype learning, producing ethical AI-ready datasets from human cell lines, and stimulating visible machine learning built on architecture maps; addressing_gaps: three entries on the black-box problem in genotype-phenotype prediction, the uncharted state of cell structure under separately applied mapping technologies, and workforce preparation
sub_elements.quality_note: Purpose and the gap it addresses are documented separately, and the gap statements are specific scientific claims rather than restatements of the purpose. The black-box entry names the deficiency and the mechanism by which this dataset answers it.

sub_elements.name: Primary Research Objectives or Tasks
sub_elements.evidence: tasks: four entries covering construction of hierarchical cell maps as directed acyclic graphs of protein assemblies across scales, interpretable genotype-phenotype learning including variant interpretation, development of visible neural networks, and integrative structure modelling of resolved protein communities using the Integrative Modeling Platform; other_tasks adding structure modelling ranked by available structural evidence and the training programme
sub_elements.quality_note: Tasks are technically specific down to the representation (directed acyclic graph of proximity-based assemblies) and the tooling, so a machine learning practitioner can tell what the data are shaped for. They are also consistent with the stated purposes rather than a second paraphrase of them.

sub_elements.name: Funding Sources and Mechanisms Listed
sub_elements.evidence: funders: three entries, two with grantor 'National Institutes of Health' covering the Bridge2AI Cell Maps for AI data generation project and the Bridge2AI Bridge Center, and one with grantor 'University of Virginia' for the Frederick Thomas Fund
sub_elements.quality_note: Both the direct data-generation award and the programme-level Bridge Center award are recorded, along with institutional support, so the funding picture is complete rather than limited to the headline grant. Each entry states the mechanism and what it supported.

sub_elements.name: Grant IDs or Award Numbers Present
sub_elements.evidence: 'Award 1OT2OD032742-01, Bridge2AI: Cell Maps for AI (CM4AI) Data Generation Project', with core project number OT2OD032742, application ID 11211616, supplement number 3OT2OD032742-01S2, principal investigator Trey Ideker, organisation University of California San Diego, project period 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31 and a fiscal year 2025 award of 5,289,382; 'Award 5U54HG012513-02, the Bridge2AI Bridge Center'
sub_elements.quality_note: Both award numbers match NIH patterns, with correct activity codes for their purpose: OT2 for an other-transaction data generation project and U54 for a centre. The record goes beyond the number to the RePORTER application id, project period and award amount, which makes the claim independently checkable, and the project period is consistent with the update horizon of November 2026.

sub_elements.name: Creators and Acknowledgements Documented
sub_elements.evidence: creators: forty-five entries, the large majority carrying ORCID identifiers and all carrying institutional affiliations across UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA (with ROR:0153tk833), Yale, UT Austin, UAB, KTH, Simon Fraser and Montreal; principal_investigator naming Trey Ideker with his ORCID; funders acknowledging the Frederick Thomas Fund
sub_elements.quality_note: Attribution is dense and machine-actionable, and the author order matches the citation exactly. One creator carries a source_caveats note disclosing that the release metadata and the preprint disagree on his affiliation, which is the kind of disclosure most records would silently resolve. The principal_investigator key is nested inside a creator entry rather than sitting at dataset level, recorded as a low-severity structural issue.

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (acquisition_methods and collection_mechanisms both populated with assay detail) and datasets shared (populated distribution_formats with a resolvable deposit URL)
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: four entries naming SEC-MS in the Nevan Krogan laboratory at UCSF, AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, immunofluorescence and confocal microscopy in the Lundberg Lab at Stanford using automated fixation and permeabilisation on a pipetting robot, and single-cell CRISPR screens with a lentiviral library targeting chromatin factors at six guide RNAs per gene in lines expressing inducible dCas9, read out with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit; data_collectors: three entries with role academic_institution
sub_elements.quality_note: Settings are named down to the laboratory, the automation and the kit, and each modality is attributed to the group that generated it. The CRISPRi entry gives the guide density and the dCas9 induction strategy, which is the level of detail a replicating laboratory would need.

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition as sub-element 1
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: four entries each with was_directly_observed: true, covering SEC-MS for proteome-wide complex mapping, AP-MS on endogenously tagged lines, ICC-IF confocal microscopy with the four channels named by their target and stain (DAPI nuclei blue, calreticulin endoplasmic reticulum yellow, tubulin microtubules red, protein of interest green) carrying was_validated_verified: true and a note that antibody quality was scored under a standard Human Protein Atlas protocol, and Perturb-seq with the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit; raw_data_sources naming the two depositing laboratories
sub_elements.quality_note: Instrumentation and reagents are specific, the observation and validation flags are set per method rather than uniformly, and the antibody quality-control protocol is named. The channel assignment in particular is the one piece of variable-level semantics the record provides.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Software-output trigger met on Element 10 fields: external_resources references code repositories at github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io, plus fairscape.github.io and integrativemodeling.org, and extension_mechanism.contribution_url points to the same repository
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: four entries covering node2vec dimensionality reduction of PPI networks, Human Protein Atlas deep-learning embedding of immunofluorescence images, contrastive integration of the two into per-protein co-embeddings with a reconstruction objective, and community detection over co-embedding similarities producing the final map hierarchy; cleaning_strategies recording CRISPR screen quality control in progress; labeling_strategies describing the two-pronged annotation against Gene Ontology and Reactome and by large language model, with data_annotation_platform 'Gene Set AI (GSAI) pipeline guiding the GPT-4 model'; machine_annotation_tools: node2vec, DenseNet-121, GPT-4 and HiDeF each with a functional description
sub_elements.quality_note: The pipeline is described stage by stage with the model architecture at each stage and the annotation confidence-scoring approach, which is well above the threshold for this sub-element. It is credited with a substantive caveat: these stages produce the computed cell maps that this release excludes, so they document the project's pipeline rather than the processing applied to the ten delivered archives. Recorded as a medium-severity content-accuracy issue, and the record's own source_caveats acknowledges drawing the descriptions from the shared MuSIC methodology.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same software-output trigger on Element 10 fields
sub_elements.evidence: machine_annotation_tools naming node2vec, DenseNet-121 (pre-trained for object recognition and applied to the four-channel confocal images), GPT-4 and HiDeF (pan-resolution hierarchical community decoding producing a directed acyclic graph); external_resources giving the Cell Mapping Toolkit as a series of Python packages at https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline with documentation at https://cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io/, FAIRSCAPE at https://fairscape.github.io under the MIT licence, and the Integrative Modeling Platform at http://integrativemodeling.org; extension_mechanism.contribution_url
sub_elements.quality_note: Tools are named with their function and the pipeline software is given as a resolvable repository with documentation and a licence, which is what the sub-element asks for. Two shortfalls: the dedicated software_and_tools slot is unused, so the information is distributed across three other slots, and no version or commit is pinned for any tool, so the pipeline is identifiable but not reproducible to a specific state.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: eleven entries, six flagged archival, covering the MassIVE mass-spectrometry deposits, the SRA BioProject, the Figshare CRISPRi atlas, the embargoed Perturb-seq components, the cm4ai.org portal, the Cell Mapping Toolkit, FAIRSCAPE and the Integrative Modeling Platform; conforms_to: RO-Crate with conforms_to_standard RO_CRATE; labeling_strategies referencing Gene Ontology and Reactome as annotation authorities; related_datasets citing both describing preprints by DOI
sub_elements.quality_note: Standards and external resources are referenced at every relevant layer: packaging (RO-Crate, FAIRSCAPE), annotation authorities (GO, Reactome), archives (MassIVE, SRA, Figshare) and literature (two bioRxiv DOIs). The archival flag usefully separates preserved deposits from live documentation.

elements.name: Dataset Evaluation and Limitations Disclosure
elements.description: Does the metadata communicate known risks, biases, or dataset limitations?

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: four typed entries, scope_limitation for the interim release lacking predicted cell maps with scope_impact stating the release suits per-dataset bioinformatics rather than integrated map analysis, coverage_limitation for the incompletely overlapping protein sets across SEC-MS, imaging and Perturb-seq, integration_limitation for the pre-publication embargo with a recommended_mitigation naming which components are expected and the quarterly update cadence, and methodological_limitation for the domain expertise required
sub_elements.quality_note: Four distinct limitation types, each typed, and two carrying forward-looking fields rather than only a statement of the problem. The coverage limitation is the most valuable disclosure: it warns that the three modalities cannot simply be joined on protein identity, which is exactly the mistake an integrating reuser would make.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: one entry with bias_type representation_bias, a description stating that data derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines do not represent all biological variants seen in the population at large, and affected_subsets naming all data in the release across MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J and their derivatives; future_use_impacts: two entries on integrating anticipated applications into data governance frameworks and on the Ethics team's tools for ethical, legal and social implications
sub_elements.quality_note: The bias is structurally categorised with a taxonomy term and an affected-subsets field, and it agrees exactly with sampling_strategies.why_not_representative, so the claim is consistent rather than isolated. Only one bias axis is categorised: the targeted 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes and the incomplete cross-modality protein overlap are documented elsewhere but never framed as selection bias, recorded as a low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: No anomalies slot. The nearest content is cleaning_strategies recording that MDA-MB-468 and undifferentiated KOLF2.1J CRISPR screen data were undergoing quality control at the time of the preprint, and the known_limitations coverage entry on incompletely overlapping protein sets
sub_elements.quality_note: No anomalies, outliers or per-file quality observations are documented for any of the ten archives: no failed-antibody counts for the imaging set, no run-level flags for the mass spectrometry, no guide dropout or low-coverage notes for the Perturb-seq atlas. The one quality signal, that QC was still in progress, describes process status rather than any finding.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present false with sensitivity_details 'CM4AI data are non-clinical, derived from tissue cultures, and are considered to be de-identified as they cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject'; content_warnings: content_warnings_present false; confidential_elements: confidential_elements_present false with details recording Human Subjects No, De-identified Samples Yes, FDA Regulated No
sub_elements.quality_note: All three slots are answered rather than omitted, and two of the three carry a stated reason for the negative rather than a bare false. A reader can tell the absence of sensitive content was assessed rather than assumed, which is the distinction this sub-element exists to capture.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: two entries, the first describing the Ethics Module's plan for ethical preparation, licensing, dissemination and Data Access supervision, balancing data openness against intellectual-property protection and against monitoring of potential commercialisation efforts, with contact_person Vardit Ravitsky (ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801) and a contact email in notes, the second naming Jean-Christophe Belisle-Pipon (ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153) of Simon Fraser University with his contact email; data_governance describing the CM4AI Data Access Committee, its access_review_process and stewardship_roles
sub_elements.quality_note: Ethics review is documented as a functioning body with a defined remit, two attributable contacts carrying ORCIDs, and a governance committee with a described review process, all of which is voluntary disclosure for a non-human-subject dataset. No conflict-of-interest statement is present, though the commercialisation-monitoring remit addresses the adjacent concern.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met via populated distribution_formats, a resolvable deposit URL and a reuse-permitting licence
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: ROR:0153tk833; citation naming 'University of Virginia Dataverse, V2'; distribution_formats access_urls at dataverse.lib.virginia.edu; retention_limit recording long-term preservation in the University of Virginia Dataverse supported by committed institutional funds
sub_elements.quality_note: A recognised institutional Dataverse instance, corroborated by the DOI prefix, the citation, the access URL and the preservation commitment, with a machine-actionable ROR for the publishing institution. The publisher slot holds only the opaque identifier with no name or repository label, recorded as a low-severity issue.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified (related_datasets carries is_described_by doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and is_referenced_by doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734) and datasets shared condition met
sub_elements.evidence: citation: full author list of forty-five names in citation order, year 2026, title, https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, repository 'University of Virginia Dataverse', version V2; doi: 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete, directly usable citation string whose author order matches the creators list exactly, carrying the DOI, the repository and the version. The two describing preprints are separately cross-referenced by DOI through typed relations, so both the data citation and the literature link are available.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to: RO-Crate; conforms_to_standard: [RO_CRATE]; conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema; conforms_to_class: Dataset; description recording that output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata in RO-Crate format under the FAIRSCAPE framework; identifier systems in use include ORCID, ROR, RRID Cellosaurus and Bridge2AI substrate and topic terms; labeling_strategies aligning maps to Gene Ontology and Reactome
sub_elements.quality_note: Conformance spans packaging, metadata schema, class and identifier systems, and the RO-Crate claim is backed by an actual metadata archive in the file inventory (cm4ai_release_metadata.zip, described as containing RO-Crate metadata and provenance graphs) rather than left as an assertion.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources describing the cm4ai.org portal as providing documentation, data releases, tools, publications and training materials, plus cellmaps-pipeline.readthedocs.io and the FAIRSCAPE tutorial and installation instructions at fairscape.github.io; existing_uses recording a virtual CodeFest in March 2024 with 38 registrants accompanied by detailed tutorials and production-ready software; other_tasks describing asynchronous virtual training, hosted virtual events and an in-person internship co-hosted at Yale and UCSD with its four-topic curriculum; page
sub_elements.quality_note: Outreach is documented as delivered activity with attendance and curriculum, not just as links: a dated training event with a participant count, a described internship programme, and three separate documentation sites for the portal, the pipeline and the packaging framework.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same datasets shared condition
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: four is_new_version_of relations to doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, F3TD5R, B35XWX and DXWOS5, one is_described_by to doi:10.1101/2024.05.21.589311 and one is_referenced_by to doi:10.1101/2024.11.03.621734, each carrying a target DOI and a title, with a note on the May 2024 release explaining where the reference was found
sub_elements.quality_note: Six relations across three relationship types, every target resolvable by DOI and every one named. The typing distinguishes version lineage from describing literature from referenced work, which is exactly the discrimination this sub-element asks for, and the relation set agrees with the release chain narrated in version_access.

strengths: Identity is corroborated five ways. The DOI prefix, the publisher ROR, the citation's repository name, the access URL and the retention statement all independently point at the University of Virginia Dataverse, and the four prior-release DOIs share the same prefix and path form. Nothing about who published this release rests on a single unverifiable field.

Numeric claims reconcile across the record. The 464 proteins imaged per condition appear identically in instances, in subpopulations and in all three imaging file descriptions; the 11,739 targeted genes appear in three slots; and total_file_count of 10 matches the file inventory exactly, with every archive carrying a listed size, a publication date and an MD5 checksum.

Conflicts and gaps are declared rather than resolved silently. The 563-versus-464 protein count across release pages is recorded with the source ranking that decided it, one creator's affiliation carries a note that the release metadata and the preprint disagree, and instances states plainly that the bundle gives the targeted gene count but not the number of profiled cells. A reader can audit every one of those decisions.

The reuse guidance is coherent and self-limiting. intended_uses, discouraged_uses and known_limitations agree that this interim release suits per-dataset bioinformatics rather than integrated cell-map analysis, and the coverage limitation warns that the three modalities interrogate incompletely overlapping protein sets, which is the specific integration mistake a reuser would otherwise make.

Collection and processing are documented to laboratory, instrument and model level: SEC-MS in the Krogan lab, immunofluorescence on a pipetting robot in the Lundberg lab with antibody quality scored under a Human Protein Atlas protocol, CRISPRi at six guide RNAs per gene with inducible dCas9 read out on the 10x 3'HT kit, and a four-stage embedding and community-detection pipeline with the model architecture named at each stage.

Ethics documentation is voluntary here and still substantive: two named review contacts with ORCIDs, a Data Access Committee with a described review process and stewardship roles, and three negative declarations on confidentiality, sensitivity and content warnings that each carry a stated reason rather than a bare false.

Funding is traceable to the record level. Both NIH awards match activity-code patterns appropriate to their purpose, and the primary award carries the RePORTER application id, supplement number, project period and fiscal year amount, making the claim checkable against an external register.
weaknesses: Format specification stops at the container. All ten archives are described as ZIPs with media type application/zip and nothing states what is inside them: no imaging format for 12.6 GB of confocal data, no mass-spectrometry format, no matrix or sequence format for the Perturb-seq atlas and no character encoding anywhere. A reuser cannot plan integration without downloading first.

The release chain is enumerated but never differenced. Five releases are named with versions, dates and DOIs, yet no errata, release notes or change descriptions say what the June 2026 release adds, corrects or withdraws relative to October 2025. For a dataset updating quarterly this is the most consequential gap.

The documented processing pipeline is downstream of the delivered files. preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools describe node2vec, DenseNet-121, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF and GPT-4 annotation, all of which produce the computed cell maps the record states this release does not contain. How the ten delivered archives were processed remains undocumented.

No variable-level metadata exists. is_tabular: false is correct, but the non-tabular equivalent is missing too: apart from the four imaging channels described in prose, nothing defines the fields of the SEC-MS elution tables, the AP-MS interaction records or the Perturb-seq count matrices.

Data quality is asserted rather than evidenced. No anomalies slot, no missing-data documentation and no per-archive quality observations: no antibody failure counts, no mass-spectrometry run flags, no guide dropout figures. The one quality signal records that QC was in progress rather than any finding.

Version numbering reads as a regression. The record carries 2.0 while listing two earlier releases at 2.1, with the citation adding V2 as a third numbering, and nothing explains that these are per-DOI Dataverse counters rather than a project-wide sequence.

External deposits are named without accessions. The MassIVE mass-spectrometry deposits, the SRA BioProject and the Figshare CRISPRi atlas are all identified in prose but carry no identifier or URL, so the raw-data trail is followable by a human search and not by a machine.

Two identifier and structural slots are used off-pattern: download_url is empty with the deposit link carried in distribution_formats access_urls, page resolves to the project release index rather than this DOI's landing page, and principal_investigator is nested inside a creator entry rather than sitting at dataset level.
recommendations: Record per-archive payload formats and a character encoding: the imaging format for the three confocal archives, the mass-spectrometry format for the SEC-MS and AP-MS packages, and the matrix or sequence format for the Perturb-seq atlas and its raw SRA package. This is the single change that would most improve reuse.

Add release notes or errata stating what the June 2026 release changes relative to October 2025, and carry that difference statement on each is_new_version_of relation so the chain can be read forwards.

Separate the processing that produced the ten delivered archives from the MuSIC map-building pipeline. Document spectral search and elution-profile scoring, image segmentation and QC, and guide assignment and count-matrix generation as this release's preprocessing, and label the embedding and community-detection stages as applying to the cell maps in future releases.

Populate anomalies and missing-data documentation with per-modality quality findings: antibody or image failure rates, mass-spectrometry run exclusions, and guide coverage or dropout in the CRISPRi atlas, so the quality claim rests on observations rather than on QC being in progress.
Give the external deposits their accessions and URLs, the MassIVE identifiers, the NCBI BioProject accession and the Figshare DOI, so the raw-data provenance trail resolves automatically.

Explain the version numbering, either by stating that version is the per-DOI Dataverse counter or by carrying the release-series designation as the version and recording the Dataverse counter separately.

Populate download_url with the Dataverse persistent URL, point page at this DOI's landing page with the project release index kept as an external resource, and lift principal_investigator out of the creator entry to dataset level.

Add selection_bias entries for the targeted panel of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes and for the incomplete cross-modality protein overlap, with affected_subsets naming the modalities each affects.
